To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The energy efficiency of YSGG: Cr3+: Nd3+ crystals can be increased by a factor of 1.5 by saturating Cr centers with a 1.06-μm laser beam.

(a) the energy efficiency of the YSGG:Nd3+ laser is improved by 1.5 times when saturable chromium centers are formed; (b) the formation of saturable chromium centers in YSGG crystals is possible using an electron beam; (c) the energy extraction efficiency is determined by the ratio of the concentration of the saturable chromium centers to the concentration of the active Nd3+ centers.

(1) the efficiency of laser action of the Cr:YSGG:Nd crystal can be increased by 1.5 times by forming Cr3+ centers absorbing at a 1.06-μm wavelength, which are saturated by the radiation of the laser, and (2) the formation of Cr3+ centers is possible by irradiation of the crystal with a laser beam at 1.06 µm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the phototropic centers on efficiency of the energy extraction from YAG:Cr:Nd crystals.
the influence of phototropic centers in YSGG on the efficiency of extraction of energy from YSGG crystals doped with Cr3+:Nd3+.

the development of new laser materials for the generation of radiation in the near IR region with the use of the 2.79-μm YAG:Nd:Cr laser as an energy source and the development of a new type of YSGG:Nd:Cr crystals for the generation of 1.3-μm radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of saturable Cr3+ centers in YSGG crystals allows one to suppress the amplified spontaneous emission, increase the energy extraction efficiency, and reduce the laser pulse duration.
the Cr3+ centers in YSGG are the most promising candidates for the development of efficient and compact lasers in the 1.06-1.1 μm range.

the use of Cr centers in the active media of lasers based on the Nd3+ ions is an effective method for increasing the efficiency of laser energy extraction and reducing the threshold of laser generation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we managed to achieve a 1.6-fold increase in energy efficiency of the YSGG: Cr3+:Nd3+:Yb3+ laser system by using the saturable Cr3+ ions.
the energy efficiency of YSGG:Nd3+ crystals can be increased 1.5-2 times by using a Cr3+ co-dopant.
the efficiency of the energy extraction from the YSGG:Nd3+ crystals can be increased by a factor of 1.5 by using the YSGG crystals with Cr3+ ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy efficiency can be improved by controlling the concentration of the phototropic centers.
saturable centers can be used to suppress the amplified spontaneous emission in a laser medium, which can be of interest for the development of high-power laser sources.
the energy efficiency of the Cr3+:Nd3+:YSGG crystal is increased by a factor of 1.5 compared to a crystal with the Cr3+ ions replaced by Y3+.
